title: Hybrid routing and cold-start cost playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This playbook documents the hybrid routing design used for kernel selection and request delegation, with a specific focus on diagnosing and containing cold-start cost spikes. It combines architecture notes, profiling and benchmarking protocols, and an operational runbook for incidents where cold-starts or kernel mis-routing produce elevated per-request GPU cost or tail latency. Intended readers: runtime engineers, oncall SREs, and release owners.

Scope and goals:
- Reduce end-to-end cold-start cost (measured as NPU-seconds per request) by providing deterministic routing fallbacks and safe kernel rollbacks.
- Provide a repeatable profiling and benchmarking procedure to reproduce cost spikes locally and in the integration lab.
- Give a prescriptive incident response runbook to bring service back within SLOs within 30 minutes.

Background and motivation:
Redwood's serving runtime supports multiple kernel variants (full-precision, quantized, sharded, fused-attention). Historically, cold-start and first-traffic routing sometimes selected kernel variants with poor warmup behaviour (large KV warmup, long memcpy paths), creating high initial GPU time and increased cost for short-lived sessions. The hybrid routing model routes at two levels:
1) Request dispatch policy (region/customer tier/capacity)
2) Slot-level kernel routing (kernel variant chosen per slot based on telemetry and heuristics)

Key design summary:
- Kernel routing is evaluated at slot creation time and re-evaluated on heavy cache-miss signals (KV-miss-ratio > 8% for first 100 tokens).
- A cold-start cost heuristic is computed as: C = warmup_time_ms * active_gpus_per_slot + additional_memcpy_ms. Threshold C > 120ms triggers a safe-fallback to the warmup-optimized kernel variant.
- Routing decisions are annotated in request traces as: route.request_policy, route.kernel_choice, route.fallback_reason. These annotations are mandatory for all traces used in automated diagnostics.

Architecture diagram (textual):
- Client -> Frontend Proxy -> Request Classifier -> Routing Fabric
  - Routing Fabric: decision engine + slot-allocator + kernel-mapper
  - Kernel-mapper consults kernel-profiles DB and active telemetry signals (recent_warmups, avg_kv_miss)
  - Slot warmup hooks call KV-prefetch and preheat allocator threads

Operational signals and SLOs to watch:
- Latency: P50 < 30ms, P95 < 110ms, P99 < 350ms (end-to-end generation request, 8-token warmup sampled)
- Cost: short-session cost (requests <= 8 tokens) should be < 0.08 GPU-seconds per request on T4-equivalent hardware equivalent (normalized)
- Warmup miss ratio: first-100-token KV-miss-ratio target < 5%
- Alerting thresholds:
  - cost_spike_alert (page): short-session 5-minute average > 0.16 GPU-seconds (2x target) OR P99 latency spike > 600ms
  - degradation_warning (email): short-session 5-minute average > 0.12 GPU-seconds (1.5x target)

Profiling methodology (how to reproduce):
1) Reproduce on a staging node that matches the customer's shard topology. Use the integration-lab runner (integration-lab v2).
2) Replay the recorded traffic sample that triggered the alert (stored as trace bundle in /integration-traces/coldstart/*.zip).
3) Enable extended kernel tracing on the slot (env DEBUG_KERNEL_TRACING=1).
4) Collect the following artifacts:
   - full runtime trace (trace.json, 10s capture)
   - kernel dispatch log (kernel-dispatch.log)
   - CUDA profiler snapshot (nvprof/ncu equivalent) of the first 2 warmup passes

CLI snippets:
- Start a local replay: 
  ./tools/replay-workload --trace /integration-traces/coldstart/customer-x-2026-01-12.zip --target staging-slot-5 --duration 60s
- Enable kernel tracing: 
  kubectl exec -it slot-5 -- /bin/bash -c "export DEBUG_KERNEL_TRACING=1; kill -HUP runtime-agent"
- Collect traces: 
  scp slot-5:/var/log/runtime/trace.json ./artifacts/trace.json

Metrics to extract and thresholds table (text):
|metric|meaning|acceptable|action if violated|
|---|---|---:|---|
|slot_warmup_ms|time until slot reports ready|< 75ms|fallback to warmup-optimized kernel|
|first_100_kv_miss_ratio|cache misses in first 100 tokens|< 5%|trigger kv-prefetch + kernel fallback|
|per_request_gpu_ms|GPU-side time per request|< 80ms (short requests)|investigate kernel memcpy paths|
|coldstart_cost_norm|normalized GPU-seconds per short request|< 0.08|page SRE if >0.16 5-min avg|

Benchmarking protocol (lab reproduction):
- Microbenchmark: kernel variants should be exercised using small-length synthetic corpus: sequence lengths = [8, 16, 64] with a 70/20/10 distribution. Run 3x and report mean and standard deviation.
- End-to-end: use the shadow traffic replayer against the full slot topology for at least 10 minutes while varying concurrency from 1 to 20. Capture GPU utilization, kernel occupancy, memcpy stalls, and slot warmup rate.
- Reproducer config (YAML example, use as template):
  cpu_workers: 8
  request_mix: "short:0.7,medium:0.2,long:0.1"
  seq_lengths: "8,16,64"
  hw_profile: "staging-t4-1x"

- Success criteria: no kernel variant produces coldstart_cost_norm > 0.08; P99 latency within 2x baseline; warmup_ms median < 60ms.

Investigations checklist (ordered):
1) Validate alert: check aggregation windows and ensure the spike is not from synthetic load.
2) Pull slot traces and kernel dispatch logs.
3) Correlate with kernel-profiles DB for recent variant rollouts.
4) Run the replay locally; if reproduced, capture nvprof/ncu for the first N requests.
5) If memcpy stalls dominate (>30% of GPU stall time), open kernel regression ticket and fall back slot mapping.
6) If KV-prefetch failure observed, force immediate prefetch and validate server-side key eviction policy.

Incident runbook (for oncall SRE):
1) Acknowledge page and add incident channel #runtime-coldstart.
2) Immediately set emergency routing to prefer warmup-optimized kernel for the affected capacity pool:
   - REST: POST /operator/v1/pools/{pool}/emergency-fallback {"kernel_family":"warmup-optimized","ttl_minutes":30}
3) If the API is unavailable, patch the slot allocator feature flag:
   kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/allocator EMERGENCY_FALLBACK=warmup-optimized
4) Collect traces (see profiling section) and attach to the incident ticket.
5) After the fallback, monitor the short-session cost and P99 for 15 minutes. If stable, start controlled roll-forward of a canary grafted with additional memcpy instrumentation.
6) Complete post-incident root cause analysis (see RCA template link in related_pages).

Rollout & CI gating checklist (pre-merge):
- Unit tests: kernel mapper and policy language parser coverage > 90%
- Integration test: replay-based regression test to assert coldstart_cost_norm for short requests
- Canary gate: deploy to 5% of pool with shadow profiling enabled for 24 hours
- Observability: route annotations and slot-level cost export enabled
